title: Normalization of the proper/open comparison under the site comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$, and set $\Lambda=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,T_1,T_2$ be Noetherian schemes (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]), let $u:T_1\to T_2$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $j_i:X\hookrightarrow T_i$ be open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] with $u j_1=j_2$. Use constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves on the small etale and pro-etale sites and their bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $A_T=\nu_T^*$ for exact comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], and let
$$e_j:A_Tj^{\mathrm{et}}_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!A_X$$
be the canonical comparison of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], applied termwise to complexes. Let
$$b_u:A_{T_2}Ru_{\mathrm{et},*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_{\mathrm{proet},*}A_{T_1}$$
be the canonical derived direct-image comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image], with its counit-mate normalization [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Properness makes $u$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, let $\alpha^e_{u,L}:j^{\mathrm{et}}_{2!}L\to Ru_{\mathrm{et},*}j^{\mathrm{et}}_{1!}L$ be the specified map [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison], and let $\alpha^p_{u,L}:j^{\mathrm{proet}}_{2!}A_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_{\mathrm{proet},*}j^{\mathrm{proet}}_{1!}A_XL$ be the canonical proper/open map [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-proetale]. To specify the named map, use the construction in that source: apply exact site-comparison pullback to the specified etale map, and identify the source by the canonical adjoint comparison for open extension by zero and the target by the counit-mate direct-image comparison followed by the open-extension comparison fixed above. Then these named maps satisfy
$$\alpha^p_{u,L}\circ e_{j_2,L}
=Ru_{\mathrm{proet},*}(e_{j_1,L})\circ b_{u,j^{\mathrm{et}}_{1!}L}\circ A_{T_2}(\alpha^e_{u,L}).$$
The equality is in $D^+(T_{2,\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$, as a map from $A_{T_2}j^{\mathrm{et}}_{2!}L$ to $Ru_{\mathrm{proet},*}j^{\mathrm{proet}}_{1!}A_XL$.

proof.text: The coefficient definition [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] gives that $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ is a finite commutative ring. Both $T_1$ and $T_2$ are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], since they are locally Noetherian. The hypothesis also makes $T_1$ quasi-compact. Applying clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] to $u:T_1\to T_2$ gives quasi-compactness of $u$ from quasi-compactness of $T_1$ and quasi-separatedness of $T_2$, and quasi-separatedness of $u$ from that of $T_1$. Thus the direct-image comparison below has all its hypotheses. No invertibility assumption on $\ell$ on these schemes is needed by that comparison.

source.place: Proof, qcqs hypotheses; schemes.tex Tags 01KV (lemma-compose-after-separated), 03GI (lemma-quasi-compact-permanence); locally Noetherian quasi-separatedness

proof.text: By [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], the specified canonical sheaf comparisons $e_{j_i,F}:A_{T_i}j^e_{i!}F\to j^p_{i!}A_XF$ are natural isomorphisms. The etale and pro-etale open-extension functors are exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]; $A$ is termwise exact comparison by [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Naturality of $e$ with respect to each differential gives an isomorphism of the termwise complexes, with the termwise inverse as inverse chain map. These exact functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms, so those chain maps descend to the displayed $e_{j_i,L}$ in the derived categories. Exactness also identifies the cohomology of an extended complex with the extension of its cohomology (kernels and images are preserved), so all open-extension inputs used below remain bounded below.

proof.text: Put $M=j^e_{1!}L$. The etale input arrow is the specified one in [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison], namely $\alpha^e_{u,L}=\varepsilon^e_{j_2,Ru_{e,*}M}\circ j^e_{2!}(\theta_{u,L}^{-1})$; [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-iso] asserts invertibility for precisely that arrow. Applying $A_{T_2}$ gives an isomorphism $A_{T_2}(\alpha^e_{u,L})$ with source $A_{T_2}j^e_{2!}L$ and target $A_{T_2}Ru_{e,*}M$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] at $M$: with its notation $a_u:A_{T_1}u_e^{-1}\cong Lu_p^*A_{T_2}$, the next arrow is $b_{u,M}$, the transpose of $A_{T_1}(\varepsilon^e_{u,M})\circ a_{u,Ru_{e,*}M}^{-1}$. Its statement asserts this particular $b$ is invertible and satisfies $\varepsilon^p\circ Lu_p^*(b_{u,M})\circ a_{u,Ru_{e,*}M}=A_{T_1}(\varepsilon^e_{u,M})$. This fixes the comparison used here, rather than choosing an isomorphism with the same ends. Finally applying $Ru_{p,*}$ to $e_{j_1,L}$ gives an isomorphism with target $Ru_{p,*}j^p_{1!}A_XL$: its inverse is the image of $e_{j_1,L}^{-1}$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph (the counit mate defining the direct-image comparison); compare the proper/open source first paragraph for the specified etale arrow

proof.text:
Now spell out the construction of the named pro-etale map specified in the statement. Its source is $j^p_{2!}A_XL$, so identifying that source with the source of the pulled-back etale arrow uses $e_{j_2,L}^{-1}$, not $e_{j_2,L}$. The construction first uses that inverse, then $A_{T_2}(\alpha^e_{u,L})$, then the named $b_{u,j^e_{1!}L}$, and then $Ru_{p,*}(e_{j_1,L})$. Hence its complete expression is
$$\alpha^p_{u,L}=Ru_{p,*}(e_{j_1,L})\circ b_{u,j^e_{1!}L}\circ A_{T_2}(\alpha^e_{u,L})\circ e_{j_2,L}^{-1}.$$
This is an expansion of the named-map construction in the statement, with every constituent supplied in steps 2 and 3. No assertion about an arbitrary isomorphism between these endpoints is used.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph and last paragraph: applying exact comparison to the etale map and identifying both endpoints; the construction is explicitly bound in this item statement

proof.text:
Compose the equation of step 4 on the right with $e_{j_2,L}$. Associativity and $e_{j_2,L}^{-1}\circ e_{j_2,L}=\operatorname{id}_{A_{T_2}j^e_{2!}L}$ cancel the final inverse pair and give exactly
$$\alpha^p_{u,L}\circ e_{j_2,L}=Ru_{p,*}(e_{j_1,L})\circ b_{u,j^e_{1!}L}\circ A_{T_2}(\alpha^e_{u,L}).$$
The source and target computed in steps 2 and 3 are respectively $A_{T_2}j^e_{2!}L$ and $Ru_{p,*}j^p_{1!}A_XL$, both in $D^+(T_{2,\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$. Thus the equality has the required type.
